package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to Android 10 (at least up to 1.1)
package_info.why_malicious: The package exposes an exported activity (TagViewer) that can be triggered by any app without permissions, allowing a rogue app to spoof NFC tag reads and present arbitrary content to the user, potentially leading to phishing, social engineering, or other attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a malicious app sends an intent)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs a fake NDEF message (e.g., a URI), crafts an intent targeting the TagViewer activity, and launches it, causing the system to display a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-controlled content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows any app to simulate an NFC tag scan and present arbitrary data to the user, bypassing the expected hardware interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only real NFC hardware events should trigger the TagViewer. Here, any app can trigger it programmatically, violating the trust boundary.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use NFC intents for testing or development, but should not be able to spoof user-facing system dialogs in production.
key_indicators: Exported activity with no permission protection
Ability to inject arbitrary NDEF messages

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a malicious app intercepts a real NFC scan)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app with intent filter for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious app intercepts NFC tag intents, modifies the tag content (e.g., changes a phone number or URL), and relaunches the TagViewer with the spoofed data, making the user believe the altered content is genuine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying NFC tag data before it reaches the intended system handler is a classic man-in-the-middle attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect the NFC tag content to be faithfully presented by the system, not altered by third-party apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or development tools may intercept intents for testing, but not in production or without user awareness.
key_indicators: Intent filter for high-priority NFC actions
Forwarding to system UI with altered content

attack_chain.action: Malicious app registers for NFC intents (e.g., NDEF_DISCOVERED) to intercept tag scans or crafts a fake intent to simulate a tag scan.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with a spoofed 'new tag scanned' dialog containing attacker-controlled data.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the spoofed tag (e.g., clicks a link, calls a number, sends an SMS), believing it to be genuine.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential phishing, social engineering, or redirection to malicious resources.

behavioral_signatures: Apps sending explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with NDEF messages
Apps registering for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED and relaunching TagViewer with modified data
Unexpected 'new tag scanned' popups without actual NFC hardware events
file_indicators: App code invoking startActivity with TagViewer component and NDEF extras
network_indicators: NDEF messages containing suspicious URLs (e.g., phishing domains)
Redirection to attacker-controlled phone numbers or SMS endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that send explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted NDEF messages, especially without a corresponding NFC hardware event. Flag apps that register for high-priority NFC intent filters and modify tag data before passing it to the system. Alert on repeated or unexpected 'new tag scanned' dialogs, especially if the device's NFC hardware was not activated.
